findings.problem: Dispatch reconciliation requires only a completed pair or rejection record; it never requires the expected provider ID to appear in an accepted PostToolBatch journal. A missing or fail-open crashed PostToolBatch therefore remains undetected for normally completed tools, and the terminal auditor has the same gap.
findings.reachable_trigger: A tool receives valid PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks, but its awaited PostToolBatch hook process crashes or is not delivered. Qwen proceeds because hook failure is fail-open; check_dispatch sees the completed pair and permits the next provider contact. Final audit also passes because completed IDs need not occur in any batch receipt.
findings.repair: Track and validate the exact provider IDs covered by accepted PostToolBatch events. Before dispatch and at terminal audit, require every expected ID to occur in exactly one batch, in addition to belonging to the disjoint completed/rejected union.

findings.problem: Cross-batch duplicate detection applies only to IDs already recorded as preexecution rejections. A completed tool ID can be replayed in multiple PostToolBatch events without fault; run-verdict likewise rejects prior derived rejections but permits duplicate completed IDs.
findings.reachable_trigger: After a tool has a completed Pre/Post pair, deliver its successful PostToolBatch payload twice. Both handler calls return continue=true, both journal rows survive terminal derivation, and the run can pass despite the contract requiring duplicate IDs to be rejected.
findings.repair: Maintain a set of every previously journaled batch tool_call_id, regardless of outcome, and reject any repeated ID in the handler. Independently reconstruct the same all-ID uniqueness rule from raw batch bytes in run-verdict.

rulings: The production file hashes match the supplied review inputs.
The exact error/invalid_tool_params/not_started tuple is narrowly recognized, while successful, started, and generic-error results cannot directly create rejection state.
Completed and rejected outcome sets are reconciled as disjoint, and rejection state is independently reconstructed from retained accepted-batch raw bytes.
The diff does not modify runtime v45 or introduce a grace window or aggregate cap.
